name: Majority Complexity of Singletons
proof: For $n=1$, the target is already known and the halving algorithm makes no query. For $n\ge2$, each coordinate is positive in just one concept, so the majority query is the all-zero hypothesis, including at $n=2$ by zero tie-breaking. Against target singleton $\{i\}$ its only disagreement is coordinate $i$. The returned positive example therefore identifies the target in one query, after which no confirmation is needed. The nontrivial initial version space requires a query, giving value one.
